summary.plain: The Beijing Spectrometer III at China's BEPCII collider, built to study hadron and tau-charm physics with the highest accuracy so far. A collaboration of about 700 members from 86 institutions in 16 countries, it began taking data in 2008 and found the charged charmonium-like state Zc(3900).
summary.technical: BESIII at BEPCII: helium-based multilayer drift chamber, plastic-scintillator TOF, CsI(Tl) calorimeter, 1.0 T superconducting solenoid and RPC muon identifier; 93% solid-angle acceptance; peak luminosity 10³³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ at 3.78 GeV; about 700 members from 86 institutions in 16 countries; first collisions July 2008; BEPCII shut down for upgrade 1 July 2024.
